draft.title: Spelling with prefixes and suffixes
card: Prefix
a word part added to the start of a word. It changes the meaning but not the spelling of the base word. Un + necessary = unnecessary, with both n letters kept.
Root
the main part of a word that carries its core meaning. In "transport", the root port means carry.
Suffix
a word part added to the end. It can change the meaning or the word class. Care + ful = careful, with only one l in -ful.
If a word ends in a silent e, drop the e before a suffix that starts with a vowel. Hope + ing = hoping. Keep the e before a suffix that starts with a consonant. Hope + ful = hopeful.
draft.remember: Build long words from parts, and check the final e before adding a suffix.

a.q: Which spelling is correct when the suffix -ing is added to the word "make"?
a.why: Make ends in a silent e, and -ing starts with a vowel, so the e is dropped: making. Makeing keeps the e, which the rule says to drop before a vowel suffix.
a.clue: Look at the first letter of the suffix.

b.q: Zara adds the prefix dis- to "appear" and the suffix -ful to "hope". Which pair of spellings is correct?
b.why: A prefix keeps the base word's spelling, so dis + appear = disappear, with one s from the prefix and one s from the word. Hope + ful keeps the e because -ful starts with a consonant. Dissappear adds an extra s, and hopful wrongly drops the e.
b.clue: Keep every letter of the base word when adding a prefix, and check what -ful starts with.

problems.detail: Why (b) says disappear has 'one s from the prefix and one s from the word', which implies two s letters. 'Appear' has no s, and disappear has only one s, from dis-. It should say the only s comes from the prefix, because appear starts with a.

check.summary: The card and both questions are correct. Why (b) wrongly says disappear has an s from the prefix and an s from the base word; appear has no s, so the word's only s comes from dis-.
